office: GlobalConnect Customer Solutions, Manila head office: floor 12 of a shared office tower
rule: Mark each point of the floor plan by who may be there. Public area: outside the office's perimeter, where anyone in the building, or a visitor not yet let in, can be. Perimeter entry point: a door in the perimeter, through which people or goods come into the office. Office area: inside the perimeter, open to all staff. Secure area: a room inside the perimeter that holds information-processing equipment, or Restricted (Tier 4) information or media, and that only named people may enter.
points: The building's shared lift lobby on floor 12. Everyone who uses the lifts passes through it.
GlobalConnect's reception desk and visitor seats. Visitors wait here until the receptionist signs them in and lets them through.
Glass doors from reception into the office. Staff open them with their badge; the receptionist opens them for a visitor.
Open-plan floor with 220 agent workstations, where every agent on shift works.
Offices of the team leaders and managers, off the agent floor.
Four meeting rooms, used by staff and by visitors with their host.
Print room and records store: the printers, and locked steel cabinets holding paper copies of clients' customers' identity documents (KYC), classified Client-Restricted.
The Manila data centre: the core network, the PBX and the call-recording servers. Only the IT staff named on its access list badge in.
Spare and returned laptops, removable media, and equipment waiting for disposal. Only the IT desk staff badge in.
Door from the service lift, for deliveries and the cleaning contractor. It opens by badge.
Fire door to the stairwell, alarmed, opening outward.
photos: The glass doors from reception into the office: a badge reader on each side, and a sign asking staff not to let anyone follow them in.
The inside of the server room door: a notice forbids photography and recording without IT approval; beside it, the sign-in sheet shows each contractor's visit with the name of the IT escort.
Two people wearing red visitor badges walk between the agent workstations; no member of staff is with them.
The corridor of the secure rooms: cameras cover the reception doors and the server room door; the IT store door, further along, has no camera on it.
The fire exit to the stairwell, wedged open with a fire extinguisher; the alarm panel beside it reads "Door alarm isolated".
Above a lifted ceiling tile at the lift lobby: the office's wall runs up to the concrete slab, with no gap to climb through.
The server room door from the corridor: plain and locked, marked only "Room 12-07"; nothing says what is inside.
An agent's desk at 19:00, after the shift has gone: the screen is locked, the desk is clear and the drawer is locked.
A meeting-room whiteboard, not wiped since yesterday's client review, lists a client's customer names and account numbers.
The server room ceiling: smoke detectors and the nozzles of the gas fire-suppression system; the cylinder's inspection tag is dated May 2026.
A water stain on a ceiling tile above rack 3 of the server room; the floor 13 staff kitchen is directly above, and no water sensor is fitted.
The server racks: front and back doors locked; a sign at the room's door says "No food or drink".
Three workstations beside the reception glass: their screens, showing customer records, face the visitor seats.
An open rack in the corridor holds the agent floor's network patch panel; it has no door, and the cables are unlabelled.
Under the server room's raised floor: power cables in one tray, network cables in a separate tray, each labelled at both ends.
The UPS panel reads "Battery OK, 32 min"; its service sticker says August 2026, and the building generator's monthly test sheet is pinned beside it.
The side of a cooling unit: its service log shows a visit every quarter by the supplier's named engineer, the last in September 2026, each signed.
A locked cage in the IT store: returned laptops and loose hard disks waiting for disposal, unlabelled, with no list of what is inside.
The IT desk's off-site device register: each laptop issued for home working, with its asset tag, holder, manager's approval and "Encrypted: yes".
A USB memory stick left in a meeting-room PC; it has no Group asset label, and IT finds it is not encrypted and not in the media register.
